title: Generalised Robust Bayes for Joint Inference of Model and Contamination
abstract: arXiv:2607.25665v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Robust generalised Bayesian methods protect parameter inference from contamination but do not generally infer its proportion or identify individual outliers. We propose H\"older--Bayes, which applies the H\"older divergence to a scaled model to construct a joint generalised posterior over model parameters and the contamination proportion, without specifying an outlier distribution. Each posterior draw flags a corresponding number of observations least compatible with the fitted model; averaging selections propagates joint uncertainty to outlier-detection scores. Under fixed, non-negligible contamination, we establish uniform boundedness of the posterior influence function, a finite-sample $n^{-1/2}$ bound on posterior-averaged excess risk, and a Bernstein--von Mises theorem. Tail overlap between the outlier distribution and the fitted model controls the population risk minimiser's bias and the associated change in limiting post

translated_title: 用于模型与污染联合推断的广义鲁棒贝叶斯方法
translated_abstract: 鲁棒广义贝叶斯方法能够保护参数推断免受污染的影响，但通常无法推断污染的比例或识别具体的离群点。我们提出了Hölder–Bayes方法，该方法将Hölder散度应用于缩放后的模型，从而在模型参数与污染比例上构建联合广义后验分布，且无需指定离群点分布。每一次后验抽样会标记出与拟合模型最不相容的相应数量的观测值；对这些选择取平均，即可将联合不确定性传播到离群点检测得分中。在固定且不可忽略的污染下，我们建立了后验影响函数的一致有界性、后验平均超额风险的有限样本 n^{-1/2} 界，以及Bernstein–von Mises定理。离群点分布与拟合模型之间的尾部重叠程度控制着总体风险最小化器的偏差以及极限后验的相应变化。
tldr: 提出Hölder–Bayes方法，通过对缩放模型施加Hölder散度来构建模型参数与污染比例的联合广义后验，在无需指定离群点分布的情况下同时实现鲁棒参数推断与离群点检测，并提供了后验影响函数一致有界、有限样本n^{-1/2}风险界及Bernstein–von Mises定理等理论保证。
en_tdlr: We propose Hölder–Bayes, which applies the Hölder divergence to a scaled model to construct a joint generalized posterior over model parameters and contamination proportion, enabling robust inference and outlier detection without specifying an outlier distribution, backed by theoretical guarantees including uniform boundedness of the posterior influence function, a finite-sample n^{-1/2} risk bound, and a Bernstein–von Mises theorem.
